premises.scope: Designated-partner actual-eigenvector curvature-transfer ladder across a balanced physical cut; for selected leverage <=1/48 gives c=(L/2)sqrt(3/5) and beta=(3/16)sqrt(3/5)L.
Completed Theorem D' relaxed 3-volume Brascamp-Lieb estimate and Theorem F diffuse exact-low-rank Fresnel estimate.
No-tau-pivot matrix class and N3 reduction; only the proved matrix inequalities are used here, not the still-open N3 density conclusion.

new_results.statement: For selected leverage <=1/48, a balanced physical cut has the actual-child/cross ledger k=0 => s3(B)>beta, k=1 => s2(B)>beta, k=2 => s1(B)>beta at c=(L/2)sqrt(3/5), beta=(3/16)sqrt(3/5)L.
If k=0 and either orientation has max 3-volume row marginal <=5/8, then ||p_Q||infinity <=128 sqrt(e/3)/L <121.842/L.
At tau=1/8192 no physical principal block on <=36 coordinates can have an eigenvalue of modulus c=(1/2)sqrt(3/5) or larger.
If the k=0 D' payment fails in both orientations, one row/column pair carries >1/4 of total squared 3-volume; at tau=1/8192 this forces at least 47,759 nonzero incident 3x3 cross minors.

For k=1,2 there are exact-three-large-eigenvalue no-pivot Hadamard lifts with selected leverage tending to zero, exactly k actual c-large child eigenvalues, exactly 3-k beta-large cross singular values, and the remaining k cross singular values tending to zero. The same family is uniformly paid by Theorem F.

newest_claude_result_applied.result: Theorem D' gives the explicit full-form bound 128 sqrt(e/3)/L in the zero-child spread-cross branch; Theorem F gives explicit 7.38334 and 7.03768 bounds on the k=1,2 Hadamard hybrid witnesses.

first_unproved_step: QFORM-DIFFUSE-HYBRID-ONE-TWO-DIRECTION-PAYMENT-v1: combine one/two ACTUAL principal child eigendirections with the complementary two/one ACTUAL cross singular directions under arbitrary spectral remainder, preserving original-coordinate product structure; or construct a genuine target counterexample.
next_mathematical_attempt: Build a remainder-stable mixed Fresnel/decoupling compiler for the k=1 and k=2 states. Use the double-heavy incident 3-volume bank when D' fails; do not assume the small complementary cross singular values are bounded below, because the Hadamard family makes them tend to zero.
